claims.text: RHEAs occupy a wide multi-principal-element compositional space with varied mixing parameters.
An integrated computational–experimental strategy can rapidly identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
First-principles calculations and machine learning can screen RHEA compositions using atomic-radius mismatch, mixing enthalpy, mixing entropy, and density descriptors.
Arc melting, homogenization, rolling, annealing, and aging can be combined as a controlled thermo-mechanical processing route for an RHEA.
The processed alloys can be mechanically tested at room temperature and at elevated temperatures.
Stepwise thermo-mechanical processing can generate multiple coherent precipitate structures in an RHEA.
The targeted microstructure contains δ-lamellae and γ″-particle-like precipitate structures.
The targeted microstructure has a refined, possibly bimodal grain structure.
Computational screening can identify composition windows in which atomic-size mismatch and mixing energetics favor coherent precipitation.
The formation of δ-lamellae followed by γ″ particles is associated with successive increases in alloy strength.
Coherent precipitates strengthen the alloy by hindering dislocation motion.
Coherent precipitate interfaces maintain ductility by allowing dislocation transmission.
Optimizing elemental makeup for lower density ensures that the resulting RHEAs are low weight.
A thermo-mechanically processed RHEA can attain an ultimate tensile strength above 2 GPa at room temperature.
A thermo-mechanically processed RHEA can attain approximately 15% tensile ductility at room temperature.
The selected RHEAs will be significantly lighter than conventional refractory alloys.
Traditional refractory alloys are typically heavy and prone to brittleness because of coarse microstructures or non-coherent precipitates.
Prediction accuracy, scale-up reproducibility, and processing kinetics limit the proposed design strategy.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements and their sensitivity to processing require systematic experimental validation.
